explanation: Both engines estimate the same permutation p-value from B random permutations, with different permutation streams and conventions (base: (k + 1) / (B + 1) with inclusive tails; DescTools: k / B). Two independent estimates differ with standard error sqrt(2 p (1 - p) / B); the rule allows four standard errors plus the plus-one convention. The JT statistic itself is compared at 1e-8.

The base engine reports a certified upper bound on the supremum over the nuisance parameter, within an absolute tolerance of 1e-8 (its default); Exact maximises on a grid with refinement and can only fall below the supremum. The rule requires Exact not to exceed the base bound and to lie within the base tolerance of it. Exact's shortfall can be larger for tables whose p-value is close to 1.
